Gram-negative cells appear pink or red at the end of Gram staining because they lose the crystal violet-iodine complex during the decolorization step. This is because gram-negative cells have a thin peptidoglycan layer and an outer membrane. After the complex is washed out, safranin, which is the counterstain, is applied. Safranin stains the decolorized gram-negative cells pink or red under the microscope.

Demand for rice is elastic when the absolute value of the price elasticity of demand is greater than 1. In the example, the elasticity is -2.5. This means that a 10 percent increase in the price of rice leads to a 25 percent decrease in the quantity demanded. When demand is elastic, a price increase will cause total revenue to decrease.

Processing cassava is necessary because it contains cyanogenic glucosides, primarily linamarin, which release hydrogen cyanide when the plant tissue is damaged. Processing reduces this hazard. Grating breaks the cells, allowing the enzyme linamarase to act on linamarin. Additionally, roasting drives off much of the remaining hydrogen cyanide. Sun-drying thin chips also lowers the cyanide content, although this is a slower process.
